references.text: Both verses describe a fire offering of pleasing aroma to the Lord (אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה), showing the pleasant fragrance of the sacrifice for God.
The priest takes a handful (קָמַץ) as a memorial portion and burns it on the altar, the same action as in the grain offering.
Describes the priest taking a handful of fine flour and oil from the grain offering, together with all the incense, as a memorial portion (אַזְכָּרָה).
Incense is placed on the breads as a memorial portion (אַזְכָּרָה) to the Lord, using the same term applied to the grain offering.
The burnt offering is described as a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the Lord (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ אִשֶּׁה לַיהוָה).
The priest burns the memorial portion on the altar, following the same practice as in the grain offering.
The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma (רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ), the first time this expression is used in Scripture.
A direct parallel confirming that the memorial portion (the handful) is the central element burned for a pleasing aroma.
Repetition of the procedure in chapter 6 confirms that the rules for the memorial offering apply consistently throughout the law.
Expands on the principle in Leviticus 2:2 by showing that the memorial portion is burned whether the grain is ground into flour or used as groats.
